title: Pupillary Light Reflex: Afferent and Efferent Defects
subject: Ophthalmology
preview: The light reflex afferent limb travels via optic nerve II; the efferent limb travels via oculomotor nerve III.
quickRevision: The light reflex afferent limb travels via optic nerve II; the efferent limb travels via oculomotor nerve III.
An efferent defect can produce poor constriction from parasympathetic pathway involvement.
Compare direct and consensual reflexes and the swinging-flashlight test for localization.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: The light reflex afferent limb travels via optic nerve II; the efferent limb travels via oculomotor nerve III.
A relative afferent pupillary defect suggests asymmetric afferent visual pathway dysfunction.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: An efferent defect can produce poor constriction from parasympathetic pathway involvement.
Compare direct and consensual reflexes and the swinging-flashlight test for localization.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A single abnormal pupil does not by itself identify whether the lesion is afferent or efferent.

quiz.question: Which nerve supplies the efferent limb of the pupillary constriction reflex?
quiz.explanation: The light reflex afferent limb travels via optic nerve II; the efferent limb travels via oculomotor nerve III.
